# Native Codex fixtures

The seven synthetic scenarios cover text, result before idle, resume, interrupt, approval withdrawal,
grouped questions, and quota/token updates. They use the installed 0.162.1 generated schema.

`probe-session`, `probe-interrupted-start`, and `probe-restart` were recorded from the installed
Windows Codex 0.162.1 executable on 2026-10-26 using `aura-cli probe codex`. The free probe passed
20 checks with zero failures and six explicit skips. No prompt or steer was sent. These recordings
prove controls and process lifecycle only; they do not prove prompted resume or turn settings.

Curation replaced home, host, session and spawn identities. Account usage and plan values,
installation identity, configured MCP server names and incidental stderr were sanitized. Native
request/response ordering and shapes remain intact. Model metadata is the public advertised catalog.
Generated goldens are reviewed outputs of the actual Rust driver running against fake pipes.

The interrupted-start recording intentionally closes before Ready. Its recorded shutdown command
and closed exit distinguish cancellation from startup failure. The replay selects the recorded
client version in `initialize` and still compares complete native request payloads.

`recorded-basic` captures one visible `Reply with exactly: ok` turn on GPT-6-Luna with low effort.
The installed CLI streamed `ok`, reported native per-turn usage and shut down normally. It has the
same personal metadata curation as the free recordings. Its golden was generated by the existing
checkpoint's replay CLI, and the current Rust suite still needs CI because Windows Application
Control refused the newly built local test executables with error 4551. CI checkpoint `e2416e7`
subsequently passed this replay and the generated schema checks on Linux and Windows.

`approval-available-decisions` is synthetic, using the restricted menu observed in the subsequent
real permission scenario. Only `accept` and `cancel` are exposed; the unsupported persistent policy
amendment is omitted. Direct attempts to send unadvertised session approval or decline are ignored.
Its expected golden was derived from `approval-withdrawal` with the two approval menus narrowed,
then verified by the actual Rust driver on Linux and Windows CI at `e2416e7`.
The stable schema permits the native `availableDecisions` extension.

The real permission smoke stopped after native allow-once failed before process creation with
`helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors`. Denial left the file absent, and allow-once also
left it absent. The original owned logs remain in ignored task scratch. The obsolete decline choice
in that recording is intentionally not presented as a passing replay of the corrected menu.
